fixed.reason: The agent deleted switchVerdict entirely and removed its call from hook.mjs, replacing the defence with a README note that settings are now writable. A Write of {env:{NODE_OPTIONS:...}} or a fake-git PATH to settings.local.json is still allowed (now by design), so the failure described still occurs; the new test even asserts that writing disableAllHooks to ~/.claude/settings.json returns null.

The settings-file detection was removed along with the whole switch check rather than broadened to CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, symlinked ~/.claude or case variants. Writes of {disableAllHooks:true} to any settings location are now allowed unconditionally, so the failure persists.

afterEdit and the parse/predict logic were deleted, not corrected. Unparseable-before, NotebookEdit and unmatched old_string edits to settings are all allowed because nothing inspects settings edits any more; the allowed-through outcome is unchanged.

hook.mjs line 31 still calls real(resolve(cwd, untilde(raw, cwd))) and paths.mjs untilde is untouched in the diff, so ~user, ~+ and ~- are still expanded shell-style while the tools expand only ~ and ~/; '~nobody/a.md' is still judged as /Users/nobody/a.md.

The new originRepo regex is anchored at the start (^(?:scheme://)?(?:user@)?github\.com[:/]...), so notgithub.com no longer matches, and it reads the URL via `git remote get-url origin`, which applies insteadOf rewrites (tests added for both). But the pattern is still case-sensitive (GitHub.com yields no slug) and has no port allowance, so ssh://git@github.com:22/owner/name.git still fails to match; those false refusals remain.

The git() helper, realGit.root/traced and the hook's catch are unchanged apart from a comment and a reworded deny message (now via unanswered()). A spawn error such as a missing git or ETIMEDOUT still throws out of traced() in an untraced repository and the catch still returns a deny, so every edit in every git repo is still refused in that state.

Instead of gating .git/, the agent added `relative(root, path).split(sep).includes('.git')` → return null, explicitly exempting .git/ from the edit gate on every branch, and rewrote the test to assert /repo/.git/config is never gated. Write to .git/config, .git/HEAD or .git/refs/heads/main on an open issue's branch is still allowed (and now also on the default branch), so the failure is unchanged or worse.

`const DEADLINE = Date.now() + 20_000` is still computed once at module load; the only change is a comment noting that each hook call is a fresh process. In-process importers such as the test suite still see every git/gh call throw once the module has been loaded for more than 20s.

findings.summary: The deadline is one module-level `let` that every `realWorld()` call overwrites, so a later world (via worldFor/readRecord/default param) silently extends an earlier world's deadline; world A made at t=0 and world B at t=19s lets A run to t=39s. findings.reason: Exactly the known in-diff bug: the first #32 fix kept a module-level let deadline that each new world restarted, stretching earlier calls. Fixed by the agent in ccc5231 by closing the deadline into each world.

findings.summary: `realGit.traced` catches every error including the 'out of time asking git and GitHub' throw and returns false, so when the marker exists only in HEAD/default branch (deleted from working tree) a timeout makes the repo look untraced and the edit gate fails open.
findings.reason: Matches the known pre-existing bug esc-traced-fails-open (traced() reads any git failure as untraced; became #34). Agent correctly noted it predates the PR and flagged it for the human.

findings.reason: Confirmed from the diff: the test never creates a second world between ticks, so it would pass with the shared `let` deadline. A real test gap that would have caught the in-diff bug; agent added the second-world check.

findings.summary: The caches `issues`, `defaults`, `origins`, `ghAliases` live for the module's lifetime, not one hook call, so in a process serving many calls stale GitHub/git state is reused.
findings.reason: Factually true but the hook runs one process per call, so no production failure follows; in-process test staleness is speculative and the spec reviewer itself called moving the caches scope creep. Not a defect the issue asked to change.

findings.summary: Duplicated empty Reads literal `{ records: () => null, add() {}, clear() {} }` appears in the test twice and elsewhere; suggest one named constant.
findings.reason: Style preference with no behavioural consequence.

findings.summary: `realWorld()` is now a ~220-line closure wrapping git adapter, GitHub adapter, caches and deadline (Divergent Change smell); suggest two factories taking shared timeLeft.

findings.summary: The deadline rationale comment sits apart from realWorld() between a typedef and its JSDoc; fold it into the JSDoc.

findings.summary: Each default parameter `world = realWorld()` now builds a fresh world (and fresh caches) on every call, so direct in-process callers re-query git/gh each time and a future caller omitting `world` loses the shared bound; undocumented.
findings.reason: Correct observation (raised by both standards and spec subagents) but the hook always passes one world per call, so no failure follows; a documentation note at most.

findings.summary: Acceptance criterion '`npm test` passes 5 runs in a row' not met as written: test/typecheck.test.mjs 'vendored declarations come from the installed Claude Code' fails (vendor 2.1.312 vs installed 2.1.314), unrelated to the diff.

findings.summary: No test pins the docs.test.mjs:331 case cited in the issue body; nothing guards against that specific regression returning.
findings.reason: Not an acceptance criterion; the new trace test covers the module-level cause. Speculative coverage wish.

findings.summary: Scope creep: the (post-round-1) diff moves the answer caches into each world although the issue asked only for the deadline; should be stated in the PR and is untested.
findings.reason: Process observation about the agent's own fix, with no defect named; the agent documented it in the PR body.

fixed.reason: The module-level `let deadline` mutated by `realWorld()` is gone; `realWorld()` now builds a per-world `const deadline = Date.now() + 20_000` and per-world `timeLeft`/`git`/`gh`/caches that close over it, so a later call's world cannot extend an earlier world's deadline. findings.summary: The Review reason lists '/code-review, mattpocock-skills:code-review' without saying which covers bugs vs standards, so a model might run only one.
findings.reason: SKILL.md already states the roles; the band reason only needs to name the skills and the order, which it does. Wording preference, no defect.

findings.summary: After round 1, runHook sets TRACE_BYPASS=1 for every hook test and dropped cwd: tmpdir(), so no end-to-end test runs the guard with the trace active and some cases depend on the checkout cwd.
findings.reason: Critique of the agent's own round-1 change to the test harness, reversing part of the round-1 advice; speculative regression scenario, not a defect in the PR.

findings.summary: The new SKILL.includes(...) assertions in trace.test.mjs duplicate a substring already pinned by assert.match and repeat the same extract-and-check in two tests; export TRACK_HINT instead.
findings.reason: Style preference about agent-added test code; no coverage or behaviour issue.

findings.summary: status.test.mjs and trace.test.mjs each declare the same top-level SKILL constant reading SKILL.md; the path is duplicated.
findings.reason: Minor duplication in agent-added test code; style only.

findings.summary: The new 'refusals and band reasons' test scans only plugins/trace/scripts/lib/, so hook.mjs and hooks/band.tsx are never checked for human-only skill names.
findings.reason: Coverage gap in a test the agent added; reviewers themselves confirm no file outside SKILL.md names those skills, so no current violation. Raised by /code-review and both round 3 subagents.

findings.summary: The forbidden-name regex runs over whole source files including comments and only matches the exact forms /implement and (implement, so it fails on harmless comments and misses forms like 'run `implement`'.
findings.reason: Precision remark on agent-added test code, not on the PR; no actual false failure or miss exists in the repository.

findings.summary: Only TRACK_HINT is checked against SKILL.md; other command hints in refusals (gh issue develop, gh issue comment) are not tied to SKILL.md.
findings.reason: Scope expansion beyond the issue (which concerns skill names and the Track hint); no defect.

findings.summary: TRACK_HINT is exported only so a test can import it, making an internal message string part of the module's API; the test no longer checks the actual refusal output.
findings.reason: Style preference about an agent-made change, and the trace tests still assert the refusal text. Also raised by the round 3 spec subagent.

findings.summary: The new test reaches SKILL.md via new URL('../../skills/trace/SKILL.md', dir) relative to lib/, which is less readable than the direct path it replaced.
findings.reason: Readability preference on agent-added test code.

findings.summary: runHook forces cwd: tmpdir() on the process while callers still pass cwd: tmpdir() in the hook input; the comment does not say the two cwds differ.
findings.reason: Comment-clarity remark; the two cwds are different things and the code is correct.

explanation.harmful: The band's Review reason in reviewWhy does not state the review base (branch's base / blocker's branch when stacked) nor the standards (GLOSSARY.md, ADRs) that SKILL.md gives. (Grader notes list 'no base in the band' as a deliberate choice; the band cannot know a stacked branch's base before a PR exists. The issue's criterion only requires the same order and the full skill name, which the diff provides.) | After a closed/merged-elsewhere PR, reviewWhy says 'review <branch>' again, contradicting SKILL.md's rule to review only the new diff after round one. (The band reason names the step, not the scope of the review; SKILL.md's round rule governs how much to review. No contradiction and no failure.) | The Read row says 'every active ADR under docs/adr/' and 'the docs/ files it links', which is broader than ADR 0007's applies-to narrowing and body-only links; row should match ADR 0007's definition. (This is the known non-bug read-row-dropped-narrowing: the merged text deliberately lists every active ADR because reading every ADR always suffices and the hooks narrow it themselves. Raised in round 1 and again in round 3 (/code-review and both subagents).)

prompt: Trace skill: runnable skill names, reads, review round cap (33c09c2..195172b, +17/-14 start; +19/-14 merged)

findings.summary: Read row's done-when cites 'the band shows the docs read', but the band reports only the main session's reads; a subagent would count Read as done and get denied. Not the hooks' per-agent test the issue asks for.
findings.reason: The issue's AC requires the done-when to be the hooks' test; the band is a main-session status display while the gate is per agent, so the row as written misdirects subagents. Confirmed by multiple reviewers citing status.mjs/hook.mjs. Repeated in round 2 (stale-commit review).

findings.summary: The review-rounds paragraph ('review only the new diff after round one') conflicts with the Review row's 'since the branch's base'.
findings.location: plugins/trace/skills/trace/SKILL.md Review row and rounds paragraph
findings.reason: The issue itself asks for both the fixed point and diff-only re-review; they describe scope for different rounds, not a real contradiction. Agent did not act on it.

findings.summary: Band's Review reason at status.mjs:115 names mattpocock-skills:code-review but omits the fixed point (branch's base) and the standards (GLOSSARY.md, active ADRs) that issue item 4 asks for at that line.
findings.reason: Issue item 4 explicitly names status.mjs:115 as needing the fixed point and standards; the diff's string lacks them, so the band and SKILL.md disagree. Verified from the diff. Repeated in round 2.

findings.summary: Read row's '(one with applies-to: only for the paths it names)' omits ADR 0007's rule that at a commit every active ADR is related, so a model skipping a scoped ADR gets denied at git commit.
findings.reason: Both reviewers quote ADR 0007's commit rule; the narrowed row misleads at the commit gate, and the final merged text indeed lists every active ADR. Repeated in round 2 against the stale commit.

findings.summary: ADR 0005's skills table and ADR 0006 step 2 still say to-tickets/implement are the pipeline's skills, contradicting the new SKILL.md which reserves them for the human.
findings.reason: Correct observation but outside the issue's scope (it names SKILL.md, refusals and band reasons only); the ADRs still accurately record which skills the pipeline reuses. Agent reasonably declined and escalated. Repeated in round 2.

findings.summary: Track refusals say `gh issue create` without a `-R <slug>` and don't mention /to-spec and /to-tickets as the human's split option.
findings.reason: Speculative (fork resolving the wrong repo) and a wording preference; not required by the issue and not acted on.

findings.summary: runHook's cwd: tmpdir() only isolates the guard tests if TMPDIR is outside any traced repo; suggests TRACE_BYPASS=1 instead.
findings.reason: Robustness preference with a contrived failure scenario (TMPDIR inside a traced checkout); the diff's approach works in practice. Agent switched to TRACE_BYPASS anyway. Repeated in round 2.

findings.summary: New rounds paragraph and the longer Read/Review rows edge toward scripting, against ADR 0005's 'skills stay short'.
findings.reason: Self-described judgement call; the issue requests this content. Repeated in round 2 against the stacked-base parenthetical.

findings.summary: The Track hint text is duplicated in two refusal strings in trace.mjs; a shared TRACK_HINT constant like BYPASS_HINT would prevent drift.
findings.reason: Style/dedup preference for two short strings, no defect. Agent applied it. Repeated in round 2.

findings.summary: Tests now pin exact hook-message wording with full-sentence regexes (shotgun surgery on rewording).
findings.reason: Acknowledged as defensible since the issue's criteria are about exact wording; a style preference. Repeated in round 2.

findings.summary: Band reason '(/code-review, mattpocock-skills:code-review)' puts two different kinds of tools in one parenthetical, unlike the single-name style elsewhere.
findings.reason: Pure style remark, self-described as minor.

findings.summary: npm test fails one test ('the vendored declarations come from the installed Claude Code', 2.1.312 vs 2.1.314); attributed to the environment, also failing on main.
findings.reason: An observation about the environment rather than a defect in the diff; it is a version-mismatch failure, not the known DEADLINE-related docs.test.mjs failure, so it does not match the pre-existing bug. Escalated to the human.

findings.summary: tdd, diagnosing-bugs, grilling and pr are named by short name in SKILL.md and the band; claims the model can only invoke them as mattpocock-skills:<name>.
findings.reason: Speculative: the issue only identified code-review as ambiguous, and the claim that short names fail is unverified. Agent had already fully qualified them in its round-1 fix; harmless but unconfirmed.

findings.summary: 'since the branch's base' is ambiguous for a stacked branch; the Review row never says the base is the blocker's branch.
findings.reason: The Branch row already defines the stacked base; a wording clarification, not a defect. Agent added a parenthetical.

findings.summary: The three-round cap gives no way to count rounds across compaction; the round number should be recorded in the progress comment.
findings.reason: An enhancement suggestion beyond the issue's requirements, no concrete defect. Agent adopted it.

findings.summary: TRACK_HINT's second use reads awkwardly: 'open an issue (...) for this change'.
findings.reason: Minor prose nit, left as is.

findings.summary: After round-1 fixes the Read row says 'every active ADR', dropping the applies-to narrowing; claims it no longer matches ADR 0007's definition and over-reads.
findings.reason: Matches the known non-bug read-row-dropped-narrowing: the final merged text says reading every ADR always suffices and the hooks narrow it themselves. Agent correctly declined to revert.

findings.summary: SKILL.md joins the two reviews with 'and' while the band says 'then'; order is only implied.
findings.reason: Trivial wording difference that does not change the order; agent changed 'and' to 'then'.

regressions.reason: The band text in status.mjs reviewWhy now reads 'mattpocock-skills:code-review since the branch's base' without naming the default branch or the blocker's branch, so it cannot misdirect a PR merged into the blocker's branch. The either-or wording only appears in SKILL.md's general Review row, not in the band hint the regression concerns.

The rewritten Read row in SKILL.md names GLOSSARY.md, every active ADR under docs/adr/, and the linked issue with its docs — generic to any traced repo. It does not mention ADR 0007 or rely on a list printed only on an issue branch.

explanation.harmful: After round-1 fixes the Read row says 'every active ADR', dropping the applies-to narrowing; claims it no longer matches ADR 0007's definition and over-reads. (Matches the known non-bug read-row-dropped-narrowing: the final merged text says reading every ADR always suffices and the hooks narrow it themselves. Agent correctly declined to revert.)
